issue.title: attachments-private store never verifies an existing remote is private before pushing attachment bytes

task_type_fields.impact: Attachment bytes believed private can be published to a public repository without any warning, while the UI labels the destination "(private)". The docs now tell users to verify visibility by hand.
task_type_fields.repro:
Root cause: `sase repo init` sidecar preflight (`preflight_sidecars` in `src/sase/sdd/_sidecar_init.py`) compares visibility only when the provider reports `status == "not_found"`, i.e. when it would *create* a missing attachments-private remote. When the remote already exists (or the hidden bare clone points at a pre-existing repo), nothing checks that the remote is actually private before `GitAttachmentStore` pushes attachment bytes to it. `describe_label()` in `src/sase/bead/attachments/upload/discovery.py` unconditionally labels the store "(private)".

Repro (code read, sase master 63bde575f0): point `repos.sidecar.builtin.attachments-private` at an existing public repository (or make the created repo public on GitHub afterwards), run `sase repo init`, then attach a file: the preflight passes, the echo says "→ <owner/repo> (private)", and the bytes are pushed to a public repo.

Found by the docs refresh agent in commit 28efa6f84c ("existing remote visibility is not verified"), which changed docs/init.md and docs/beads.md to tell users to verify an existing remote's visibility themselves; re-verified by the sase-1ck (bead note attachments) land agent. sase-1ck's plan scoped the visibility preflight to creation only.

Fix: once sase-1d5 lands its anonymous remote-visibility probe (`remote_visibility`, sase-1d5.3/1d5.4), run it for the attachments-private remote in repo-init preflight, the `project.attachment_store` doctor check, and before the first upload per process; refuse or warn when it reports `public`, and stop hard-coding the "(private)" label.

issue.creation_reason: Found by docs commit 28efa6f84c and re-verified while landing epic sase-1ck: repo-init preflight checks visibility only for a remote it would create, so bytes labeled private can land in a public repo.
